finalText:
Five files, all in `src/`, no framework — just Node's built-in `http`. Here's how a request flows through it:

```mermaid
graph LR
  server.js -->|checks token| auth.js
  server.js --> routes.js
  routes.js -->|reads| cache.js
  cache.js --> store.js
  routes.js -->|writes| store.js
```

- **`server.js`** — the entry point. Starts an HTTP server, checks the `Authorization` header with `auth.js`, and hands anything that passes to `routes.js`. No token, no entry: 401.
- **`auth.js`** — bearer tokens shaped like `<userId>.<signature>`, signed with HMAC using an `AUTH_SECRET` env var (or a dev fallback).
- **`routes.js`** — a small table mapping `METHOD /path` to a handler: `GET /users`, `GET /orders`, `POST /orders`. Reads go through the cache, writes go straight to the store.
- **`cache.js`** — a 256-entry LRU sitting in front of the store, just to absorb repeat reads. No expiry logic of its own.
- **`store.js`** — the actual data, kept in memory. Every record expires 15 minutes after it was last written, so it's really a stand-in for a database.

There's no `package.json`, tests, or config files in the repo — just these five files, so this is the whole thing.
